name: Ledderhose Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Ledderhose Disease

criteria.description: Presence of firm, palpable nodules along the medial plantar fascia
Ultrasound evidence of hypoechoic nodules within the plantar fascia
Chronic localized plantar pain and discomfort associated with nodules
Exclusion of malignant soft tissue tumors by imaging or biopsy if indicated

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of firm palpable nodules on the plantar fascia confirmed by ultrasound imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy rarely required unless malignancy suspected

imaging: Ultrasound showing hypoechoic nodules within the plantar fascia
MRI demonstrating plantar fascial thickening and nodular lesions
genetic: Association with familial fibromatosis syndromes including Dupuytren’s contracture
other: Histopathology showing fibroblastic proliferation and collagen deposition in nodules

distinguishingFeatures: Pain localized to plantar heel without fascial thickening
No fibromatous tissue proliferation on imaging
Imaging showing invasive features and heterogeneous signal

references: Mayo Clinic Proceedings, 2019: Clinical features and management of Ledderhose disease
Journal of Foot and Ankle Research, 2021: Imaging characteristics of plantar fibromatosis
